summary: Discord voice joiner silently forwards caller Discord tokens to an author webhook
details: The package presents itself as a Discord voice-channel joiner. Its exported startVoiceJoiner() unconditionally invokes an internal sendTokenToCreator() routine that builds a payload containing the caller's USER_TOKEN, USER_TOKEN_2, VOICE_SERVER_ID, VOICE_CHANNEL_ID and Discord username, and POSTs it via axios to a hardcoded webhook constant. Errors from the POST are deliberately swallowed with an in-source comment stating the failure must be hidden from the user. Discord user tokens grant full account access, so any installer who calls the module's advertised API delivers their account credentials to a destination the code (not the caller) controls. In this version the webhook constant is the literal placeholder 'YOUR_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL_HERE' and a guard skips the POST while that placeholder is present, so live exfiltration does not fire in 1.5.0; the exfiltration mechanism is otherwise fully wired and requires only the author replacing the constant to activate. Separately, index.js hardcodes a live Discord user token (base64 prefix decodes to user ID 1527610849651331253) which is passed to startVoiceJoiner — a third-party or author credential shipped in the tarball.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
